```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Saporta 2026 extended the afabicin pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD)
model of Saporta 2024 to immunocompetent mice. The drug-effect structure for
afabicin desphosphono, the active moiety of the FabI-inhibitor prodrug
afabicin, was kept. A neutrophil-mediated immune response was added in the
thigh, and the model was fitted jointly to the earlier in vitro time-kill data
and to new immunocompetent mouse thigh infection data from five
*Staphylococcus aureus* strains.

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Saporta_2026_afabicin_invitro_mouse"))

# The model has no inter-experiment variability, so only the residual error is
# zeroed for typical-value simulations.
mod_tv <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, "sigma")

# With no omega, rxode2 notes that a multi-subject solve has no between-subject
# variability. That is expected here and is muffled; any other warning shows.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("multi-subject simulation without", conditionMessage(w))) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
solve_df <- function(model, ev, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, ev, ...)),
    warning = muffle_no_omega
  )
}
```

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00959-25>
* PubMed Central open-access copy: <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13041350/>
* Sibling models: `Saporta_2024_afabicin_invitro` and
  `Saporta_2024_afabicin_invitro_mouse` (in vitro and neutropenic mouse thigh;
  see the Saporta 2024 article).

## Structure

The model carries two bacterial systems side by side, as the authors fitted
them jointly:

* **In vitro** (`log_cfu_invitro`, `dvid = 1`): growing drug-susceptible
  bacteria `bact_s` and dormant bacteria `bact_d`, driven by a static bath
  concentration dosed into `afabicin_desphosphono` (mg/L).
* **Thigh** (`log_cfu_thigh`, `dvid = 2`): `bact_s_thigh`, `bact_d_thigh` and
  a phagocytosed state `bact_phagocytosed_thigh`, driven by the unbound plasma
  concentration `fu * CP_AFABICIN_DESPHOSPHONO_MGL` with `fu = 0.02`.

Transfer from S to D is `kSD = (S + D) * (kgrowth - kdeath) / Bmax`. Afabicin
desphosphono kills only S bacteria through a sigmoid Emax model with
`EC50 = beta * MIC^gamma`, and an adaptation pair (`aroff` -> `aron`, onset
`kon * C`, offset `koff`) lowers Emax as `Emax * (1 - ASon / (ASon + AS50))`.
In the thigh, Emax is `Emax vitro * RatioEmax` and `beta` has its own in vivo
value. Model time zero is the time of infection; treatment started 2 h later.

Neutrophils follow a fixed Friberg maturation chain (`prol`, `transit1` to
`transit3`, `circ`) and move into the thigh (`neut_thigh`) at the transit
rate `ktr = 4 / MTT`, amplified after infection by the surge
`1 + Namp / (((T - NT0) / NSW)^6 + 1)`. Neutrophils phagocytose S and D
bacteria at `kphag = kphag,max * (1 - (P/N)^H / ((P/N)^H + (P/N50)^H))`, where
P/N is the ratio of phagocytosed bacteria to thigh neutrophils. Phagocytosed
bacteria are digested at `kdig = kphag,max` and still count as CFU until then,
because phagocytes were lysed before plating.

## The mouse PK is a user-supplied input

Supplementary text 2 prints the structure of the mouse PK model that produced
the plasma concentrations (an intraperitoneal depot, one absorption transit
compartment and a two-compartment afabicin desphosphono model), but no
published source reports its parameter values. The thigh system therefore
reads the total plasma concentration from the time-varying covariate column
`CP_AFABICIN_DESPHOSPHONO_MGL` (mg/L). Set it to 0 for growth controls and for
records that only simulate the in vitro system.

# Population

```{r population}
str(mod$population)
```

The in vivo data are 819 immunocompetent female ICR or Swiss Webster mice
infected intramuscularly in the thigh with one of five *S. aureus* strains
(Supplementary Table S1; afabicin desphosphono MIC 0.004 to 0.06 mg/L).
Afabicin 0.011 to 150 mg/kg was given intraperitoneally every 6 h from 2 h
after infection; one strain (IHMA 1073118) was studied in controls only. Thighs
were harvested 2 to 74 h after infection. The in vitro arm re-uses the static
time-kill data described in Saporta 2024.

# Source trace

## Equations

| Model element | Source location |
|---|---|
| S, D and P bacterial states, kSD from S + D and Bmax | Eqs 2-4; Figure 1 |
| Saturable phagocytosis on the P/N ratio | Eq 5; Results, 'Model for immune response' |
| kdig equal to kphag,max, not saturable | Results ('No saturation of the digestion process'; 'kdig could share the same estimate') |
| Neutrophil maturation chain with feedback exponent 0.149 | Supplementary text 1 |
| Recruitment surge into the thigh, from the time of infection | Eq 1; Supplementary text 1; Figure S1 |
| Every neutrophil state starts at Ncirc,T0 | Supplementary text 1 |
| EC50 = beta * MIC^gamma | Eq 6 |
| Drug effect on S only | Materials and Methods, 'PKPD modeling of afabicin desphosphono activity' |
| Sigmoid Emax with adaptation (ASoff / ASon, AS50) | Materials and Methods; Figure 1; structure of Saporta 2024 Eqs 3-5 |
| Emax vivo = Emax vitro * RatioEmax | Table 1 |
| ATCC 33591 inoculum bioavailability | Table 1; Results, 'Model for immune response' |
| Unbound driver, fu = 0.02 | Supplementary text 2 ('Unbound concentrations from Central'); value from Saporta 2024 Methods |
| Additive error on log10 counts per setting | Materials and Methods, 'Data analysis and software'; Table 1 footnote a |

## Parameters

```{r param-trace}
ini_tab <- mod$iniDf |>
  filter(!is.na(ntheta)) |>
  transmute(parameter = name, value = signif(est, 4), fixed = fix, label)
knitr::kable(ini_tab, caption = "ini() values. Log-scale entries back-transform to the Table 1 values listed in the model file's source-trace comments.")
```

| Parameter | Table 1 value | Model entry |
|---|---|---|
| kgrowth | 1.10 /h (fixed) | `lkgrowth` |
| kdeath | 0.179 /h (fixed) | `lkdeath` |
| Bmax vitro / vivo | 9.86 log10 CFU/mL / 9.08 log10 CFU/g (fixed) | `lbmax`, `lbmax_thigh` |
| RES vitro / vivo | 0.877 / 0.555 log10 | `addSd_log_cfu_invitro`, `addSd_log_cfu_thigh` |
| F33591 | 0.437 | `finoc_atcc33591` |
| Ncirc,T0 | 6.23 log10 N/mL (fixed) | `lcirc0` |
| MTT | 37.7 h (fixed) | `lmtt` |
| Namp, NT0, NSW | 44.2, 50.5 h, 28.2 h (fixed) | `lnamp`, `lnt0`, `lnsw` |
| kphag,max = kdig | 0.963 /h | `lkn_max` |
| P/N50 | 114 CFU/N | `lpn50` |
| H | 0.475 | `lhill_pn` |
| Emax vitro | 2.99 /h | `lemax` |
| RatioEmax | 0.0796 | `lratio_emax_thigh` |
| beta vitro / vivo | 1 (fixed) / 0.182 | `lec50`, `lec50_thigh` |
| gamma | 0.185 | `e_mic_ec50` |
| Hill | 0.515 | `lhill` |
| kon | 0.556 mL/(ug h) | `lkon` |
| koff | 0.0139 /h (fixed) | `lkoff` |
| AS50 | 0.784 | `lar50` |
| Feedback exponent | 0.149 | `lgamma` (Supplementary text 1) |
| fu | 0.02 | `fu` (Saporta 2024) |

# Checks against values stated in the text

The Results and Abstract quote derived quantities that follow from Table 1:
an in vivo Emax of 0.24 /h against 2.99 /h in vitro, an EC50 about 80%
(Abstract: 82%) lower in vivo, and a baseline circulating neutrophil count of
1.69 x 10^6 /mL (Prediction of clinical efficacy).

```{r text-checks}
th <- setNames(mod$iniDf$est, mod$iniDf$name)
chk <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("Emax vivo (1/h)", "EC50 reduction in vivo (%)", "Ncirc,T0 (cells/mL)"),
  model = c(
    exp(th[["lemax"]] + th[["lratio_emax_thigh"]]),
    100 * (1 - exp(th[["lec50_thigh"]] - th[["lec50"]])),
    exp(th[["lcirc0"]])
  ),
  paper = c(0.24, 82, 1.69e6)
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model - paper) / paper)
knitr::kable(chk, digits = 3)
# The paper rounds to two or three significant figures.
stopifnot(all(abs(chk$pct_diff) < 2))
```

# Neutrophil dynamics

Without a cytotoxic drug the maturation chain stays at its baseline, so the
circulating count is constant and only the thigh pool moves, following the
recruitment surge of Figure S1 (peak at 50.5 h after infection).

```{r neutrophils}
ev_ctrl <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = seq(0, 120, by = 1), evid = 0L, dvid = 2L,
  CP_AFABICIN_DESPHOSPHONO_MGL = 0
)
sim_neut <- solve_df(mod_tv, ev_ctrl, params = c(linoc_thigh = log(10^7.36)))

ggplot(sim_neut, aes(time, neut_thigh / exp(th[["lcirc0"]]))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after infection (h)",
    y = "Thigh neutrophils / baseline circulating count",
    caption = "Compare with Figure S1 of Saporta 2026 (surge function)."
  )

stopifnot(
  # The feedback chain holds Ncirc at baseline in the absence of drug.
  max(abs(sim_neut$circ / exp(th[["lcirc0"]]) - 1)) < 1e-6,
  # Thigh neutrophils peak a few hours after the surge peak, delayed by the
  # 1 / ktr = 9.4 h residence time.
  sim_neut$time[which.max(sim_neut$neut_thigh)] > 50.5,
  sim_neut$time[which.max(sim_neut$neut_thigh)] < 70
)
```

# Growth controls against Supplementary Table S2

Supplementary Table S2 lists the median observed count of every untreated
control group. Each group is simulated from its own inoculum (time 0), with the
F33591 inoculum bioavailability applied to the ATCC 33591 groups. Growth does
not depend on the MIC, so the strains differ only through that flag.

```{r controls-plot, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = "Typical-value growth-control predictions (lines) against the Supplementary Table S2 medians (points), coloured by inoculum size. Compare with the control panels of Figure 2 and Figure S2 of Saporta 2026."}
ggplot(sim_ctrl, aes(time, log_cfu_thigh, colour = factor(inoc))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = ctrl_obs, aes(time, obs)) +
  facet_wrap(~strain) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after infection (h)", y = "Thigh count (log10 CFU/g)",
    colour = "Inoculum (log10 CFU/g)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r controls-check}
ctrl_cmp <- ctrl_obs |>
  left_join(groups, by = c("strain", "inoc")) |>
  left_join(sim_ctrl |> select(id, time, pred = log_cfu_thigh), by = c("id", "time")) |>
  mutate(resid = obs - pred)

ctrl_cmp |>
  group_by(strain) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    median_resid = median(resid),
    median_abs_resid = median(abs(resid))
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !n, ~ round(.x, 2))) |>
  rename(
    "Strain" = strain, "Medians compared" = n,
    "Median (obs - pred)" = median_resid,
    "Median |obs - pred|" = median_abs_resid
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Growth-control medians (Table S2) against typical-value predictions, log10 CFU/g.")

overall <- ctrl_cmp |>
  summarise(
    median_resid = median(resid),
    median_abs = median(abs(resid)),
    q90_abs = quantile(abs(resid), 0.9)
  )
knitr::kable(overall, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  # Centre: an error in kphag,max, P/N50, the surge or Bmax shifts every
  # control group by most of a log10 unit.
  abs(overall$median_resid) < 0.35,
  overall$median_abs < 0.5,
  # Envelope: the low-inoculum groups the paper flags as highly variable
  # (up to 4 log10 at 50 h) sit in the upper tail.
  overall$q90_abs < 1.5
)
```

The typical-value curves follow the control medians across strains and
inoculum sizes. The largest residuals are in the lowest-inoculum groups
(about 6 log10 CFU/g), where the paper reports observations spanning up to
4 log10 CFU/g at 50 h and notes that the model, without variability in the
immune response, cannot capture all of them.

# Contribution of the immune response

Setting `kphag,max` near zero removes phagocytosis while keeping the bacterial
growth parameters, giving the corresponding neutropenic-like growth curve.
Bacteria then grow toward Bmax (9.08 log10 CFU/g); the neutrophil response
holds counts about one log10 lower and turns them down as the recruitment
surge peaks.

```{r immune-contribution}
ev_one <- ev_ctrl |> filter(time <= 74)
sim_immune <- bind_rows(
  solve_df(mod_tv, ev_one, params = c(linoc_thigh = log(10^7.36))) |>
    mutate(scenario = "Immunocompetent (final model)"),
  solve_df(mod_tv, ev_one, params = c(linoc_thigh = log(10^7.36), lkn_max = log(1e-8))) |>
    mutate(scenario = "No phagocytosis")
)
ggplot(sim_immune, aes(time, log_cfu_thigh, linetype = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 9.08, colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Time after infection (h)", y = "Thigh count (log10 CFU/g)", linetype = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

at74 <- sim_immune |>
  filter(time == 74) |>
  select(scenario, log_cfu_thigh)
knitr::kable(at74, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  at74$log_cfu_thigh[at74$scenario == "No phagocytosis"] -
    at74$log_cfu_thigh[at74$scenario == "Immunocompetent (final model)"] > 0.5
)
```

# Afabicin effect in the thigh under constant exposure

Without the mouse PK, source Figures 2 and 3 (treated groups) cannot be
replicated. Holding the unbound concentration constant from 2 h after
infection shows the drug-effect parameters directly. The in vivo Emax is
0.24 /h, so even at saturating exposure the kill rate on S bacteria is below
the net growth rate (`kgrowth - kdeath` = 0.92 /h); the decline in counts
comes from the drug effect and the phagocytosis together. The in vivo EC50 at
an MIC of 0.008 mg/L is `0.182 * 0.008^0.185` = 0.075 mg/L unbound.

```{r thigh-constant}
cu_levels <- c(0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1)
ev_cu <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_along(cu_levels), time = seq(0, 74, by = 1)) |>
  mutate(
    evid = 0L, dvid = 2L, cu = cu_levels[id],
    CP_AFABICIN_DESPHOSPHONO_MGL = ifelse(time >= 2, cu / 0.02, 0)
  )
sim_cu <- solve_df(mod_tv, ev_cu, params = c(linoc_thigh = log(10^7.36)), keep = "cu")

ggplot(sim_cu, aes(time, log_cfu_thigh, colour = factor(cu))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after infection (h)", y = "Thigh count (log10 CFU/g)",
    colour = "Unbound C (mg/L)",
    caption = "MIC 0.008 mg/L (ATCC 29213), inoculum 7.36 log10 CFU/g. Constant exposure is illustrative, not an afabicin dosing regimen."
  )

cu74 <- sim_cu |>
  filter(time == 74) |>
  arrange(cu)
knitr::kable(cu74 |> select(cu, log_cfu_thigh), digits = 2)
# Deterministic solve: killing increases monotonically with exposure.
stopifnot(all(diff(cu74$log_cfu_thigh) < 0))
```

# The in vitro arm

The in vitro system shares `gamma`, `Hill`, `kon`, `koff` and `AS50` with the
thigh. A growth control approaches Bmax vitro (9.86 log10 CFU/mL), and static
concentrations around the in vitro EC50 at an MIC of 0.008 mg/L
(`0.008^0.185` = 0.41 mg/L) produce graded responses: delayed growth or
early killing followed by regrowth as adaptation builds at the lower
concentrations, and sustained killing at the highest.

```{r invitro}
conc_levels <- c(0, 0.1, 0.4, 1.6, 6.4)
ev_vitro <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    id = seq_along(conc_levels), time = 0, evid = 1L,
    cmt = "afabicin_desphosphono", amt = conc_levels
  ),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_along(conc_levels), time = seq(0, 240, by = 1)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  mutate(CP_AFABICIN_DESPHOSPHONO_MGL = 0) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_vitro <- solve_df(mod_tv, ev_vitro) |>
  mutate(conc0 = conc_levels[id])

ggplot(sim_vitro |> filter(time <= 48), aes(time, log_cfu_invitro, colour = factor(conc0))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "In vitro count (log10 CFU/mL)", colour = "C (mg/L)")

ctrl_vitro <- sim_vitro |> filter(conc0 == 0, time == 240)
stopifnot(abs(ctrl_vitro$log_cfu_invitro - 9.86) < 0.05)
```

# Human projection (source Figure 4)

The paper projected the model to patients with a human population PK model of
afabicin (Supplementary Table S3), assuming human neutrophils are as potent as
murine ones, and varied only the baseline neutrophil count (1.69 x 10^6 or
5 x 10^6 /mL). That PK model is printed as a parameter table without its
equations (see Assumptions and deviations), so it is not packaged here.
The immune-response part of the projection can still be shown. Raising
`lcirc0` to the human value gives the untreated course of a 7 log10 CFU/g
infection; the paper notes that the immune response alone does not reach the
bacterial killing achieved with afabicin.

```{r human-immune}
ev_h <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = seq(0, 96, by = 1), evid = 0L, dvid = 2L,
  CP_AFABICIN_DESPHOSPHONO_MGL = 0
)
sim_h <- bind_rows(
  solve_df(mod_tv, ev_h, params = c(linoc_thigh = log(1e7), lcirc0 = log(1.69e6))) |>
    mutate(baseline = "1.69 x 10^6 /mL"),
  solve_df(mod_tv, ev_h, params = c(linoc_thigh = log(1e7), lcirc0 = log(5e6))) |>
    mutate(baseline = "5 x 10^6 /mL")
)
ggplot(sim_h, aes(time, log_cfu_thigh, colour = baseline)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 24, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after infection (h)", y = "Bacterial count (log10 CFU/g)",
    colour = "Baseline neutrophils",
    caption = "Untreated course; the dashed line marks the source Figure 4 treatment start (24 h)."
  )

h96 <- sim_h |>
  filter(time == 96) |>
  arrange(baseline)
# More neutrophils, more phagocytosis: the higher baseline ends lower.
stopifnot(h96$log_cfu_thigh[2] < h96$log_cfu_thigh[1])
```

# PKNCA

The model carries no PK. The in vitro concentration is static and the mouse
plasma concentration is an external input, so there is no concentration-time
profile for non-compartmental analysis. Validation instead relies on the
closed-form checks, the neutrophil steady state, the growth-control comparison
against Supplementary Table S2 and the structural checks above. `PKNCA` is
loaded only for consistency with the other articles.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Mouse PK not encoded.** The mouse PK model (Bader 2017, a conference
  poster) has unpublished parameter values, so the thigh system takes the
  total plasma concentration `CP_AFABICIN_DESPHOSPHONO_MGL` as a time-varying
  input. The treated-group panels of Figures 2 and 3 cannot be replicated.
* **Unbound fraction from Saporta 2024.** Saporta 2026 states that unbound
  concentrations drove the effect but does not repeat the value; `fu = 0.02`
  is taken from the Saporta 2024 Methods, which used the same PK model and
  effect structure.
* **Human PK model not packaged.** Supplementary Table S3 lists the values of
  the human afabicin / afabicin desphosphono PK model used for Figure 4
  (built from Phase I data, not otherwise published) but not its equations.
  The reference height and weight of the linear covariate effects, the form
  and reference dose of the dose effect on the oral bioavailability logit,
  whether the oral transit and absorption feed afabicin or afabicin
  desphosphono, and the human unbound fraction are not reported, so the
  human projection cannot be rebuilt from the source.
* **F33591 value.** Table 1 gives 0.437 for the final model; the Results quote
  0.458 from the immune-response model before the drug-effect parameters were
  re-estimated jointly. The Table 1 value is used.
* **Strain and inoculum are design inputs.** `mic` / `mic_thigh` default to
  0.008 mg/L (ATCC 29213), `linoc_thigh` to 7.2 log10 CFU/g (the middle of the
  7.14 to 7.36 treated-group inocula in Table 2) and `linoc` to 6 log10 CFU/mL.
  `strain_atcc33591 = 1` applies the F33591 inoculum bioavailability. Override
  these with `rxSolve(params = ...)`, per id where needed.
* **beta is carried as the EC50 at an MIC of 1 mg/L** (`lec50`,
  `lec50_thigh`), as in the Saporta 2024 models, and `gamma` as
  `e_mic_ec50`. The feedback exponent 0.149 is printed in Supplementary text 1
  rather than Table 1 and is fixed.
* **Units of P/N.** P is in CFU/g of thigh and the neutrophil count in
  cells/mL; the ratio is used as printed (P/N50 = 114 CFU/N).
* **Limit of detection not modelled.** The paper does not describe a
  censoring method, and the model returns uncensored log10 counts.
